description: Measured results of a private, local-only legal RAG system — hybrid retrieval with reranking, cited answers, refusal discipline, ethical walls. Benchmarks honest, failures included.

readme.text:
# Sovereign Legal RAG — Results **Private document intelligence for legal teams, running entirely on hardware the firm controls.** This repository publishes what the system achieves — measured retrieval quality, real sample behavior, and honest limitations. The engine itself (code, prompts, pipeline, and tuning) is private and deployed for clients. > Built by [MushiSenpai](https://theinvalid.me) as the application layer of the > [Sovereign AI Deployment](https://theinvalid.me/services) offer. Everything > below was measured on **real public legal data** (expert-annotated commercial > contracts), so the numbers are on the kind of documents a firm actually has — > not toy data. --- ## What it does - **Hybrid retrieval with reranking** — semantic search *and* exact-term search (defined terms, party names, `Section 12.4(b)`) fused into one ranked list, then reranked for precision. Lawyers search both ways; the system catches both. - **Pinpoint citations** — every answer cites `[document, page/section]`. - **Refusal discipline** — answers only from retrieved text; when the documents don't contain the answer it says exactly that, instead of inventing. - **Ethical walls** — a user retrieves only documents in matters they're cleared for; walled documents can't surface in an answer *or* a citation. - **Tamper-evident audit** — every query, role, and surfaced document is logged to an append-only, hash-chained audit log. - **Local-only, zero egress** — no cloud API, no per-token bills. The only network call is to the firm's *own* LLM endpoint. Unplug the network; it still answers.

--- ## Measured retrieval quality 150 clause-localization questions over real, expert-annotated commercial contracts (CUAD v1). A **hit** = a retrieved chunk contains the annotated answer span. Numbers are from a real run; full tables and method in [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md). | mode | MRR | R@1 | R@5 | R@10 | |---|---|---|---|---| | semantic only | 0.4337 | 0.3067 | 0.5867 | 0.7667 | | keyword only | 0.5512 | 0.3933 | 0.7467 | 0.86 | | hybrid | 0.5307 | 0.38 | 0.7667 | 0.86 | | **hybrid + rerank** | **0.5639** | **0.44** | 0.74 | 0.8467 | Three findings worth more than the headline number: 1. **Semantic-only search — the standard "chat with your PDFs" recipe — is the weakest mode on legal text.** Clause language is exact-term heavy; a pure vector search misses what a lawyer actually types. 2. **Fusion alone isn't magic** — plain hybrid trails keyword search on MRR here. It's the reranking pass that converts fused recall into top-rank precision (best MRR and R@1 of all modes). 3. **Reranking trades a little deep recall (R@10) for precision at rank 1** — the right trade for cited answers built from the top few passages. **Vision retrieval (experimental tier):** retrieving over rendered *page images* — no OCR, no text parsing — beat text hybrid retrieval on a 120-question page-level eval, **MRR 0.6489 vs 0.5208**. Full table in [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md#vision-retrieval-page-level-120-questions). --- ## See it run Terminal proof — local endpoints, ethical walls, a grounded cited answer: ![Terminal demo: local-only endpoints, ethical walls, cited answer](assets/airgap.gif) Split screen — cited query · hash-chained audit log · external egress staying flat: ![Split-screen demo: cited query, audit log, zero egress](assets/splitscreen.gif) The retrieval-mode comparison UI — the same query through all four modes, side-by-side, with expandable cited passages: ![Web UI demo: one query, four retrieval modes compared](assets/webui.gif) --- ## Sample behavior (captured live) Real transcripts, verbatim, in [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md#sample-behavior-captured-live): - Two retrievals with pinpoint citations — an *indemnification obligations* question landing on the contract's indemnification section, and a *governing law* question landing on `25. APPLICABLE LAW`. - A **correct refusal**: a `compliance` role asks about a walled matter → the ethical wall returns zero sources → the system replies *"I could not find this in the provided documents."* — without ever calling the LLM — and the audit log records the query with `n=0`. --- ## Honest limitations - **R@1 is 0.44.** The top-ranked chunk contains the annotated span 44% of the time; the system answers from the top *k* passages, not just rank 1, and cites so a lawyer can verify. This is measured retrieval, not a marketing claim. - The eval measures **clause localization (retrieval)**, not end-to-end answer correctness — grounding is enforced by design (citations + refusal), but generation quality is not separately scored here. - One corpus (English commercial contracts), one run, 150/120 questions. No cross-corpus or statute-heavy eval yet. - Vision retrieval numbers are **proof-of-concept scale** and need a GPU; it's an optional tier, not the default path. - Hybrid *without* reranking underperformed keyword search on MRR on this corpus — kept in the table because that's the point of measuring. --- ## What's *not* in this repo The engine is the product: source code, prompt templates, chunking and fusion parameters, model choices, the ingestion pipeline, and the eval harness are private. This repo is the measured record of what that engine does. **Want it on your own documents?** It's available as a private deployment — [theinvalid.me/services](https://theinvalid.me/services). I'll run a small slice of your non-sensitive files as a capability demo before any commitment. --- ## Data attribution & license Eval ground truth: [CUAD v1](https://www.atticusprojectai.org/cuad) (The Atticus Project), CC BY 4.0 — expert clause annotations over public commercial contracts. **License: All rights reserved. Benchmarks and findings shared for transparency.**
